title: Lesson Plan — Timeline and Sources of History (Class 6 CBSE Social Science)
subject: Social Science
objectives: Define a timeline and explain what it shows (order, duration, simultaneity).
Use BCE and CE correctly, including the no-year-zero rule.
Convert between decade, century and millennium.
Place events in the broad periods Ancient / Medieval / Modern of Indian history.
Distinguish archaeological, literary and oral sources with examples.
Explain stratigraphy and radiocarbon dating in their own words.
prerequisites: Knowledge of basic numbers and subtraction.
Familiarity with calendars and the current year.
Comfort with simple maps of India.
materials: Long strip of paper (or rope) for a class timeline on the floor / wall
Sticky notes for events to be placed
Pictures of: a coin, a piece of pottery, a Vedic manuscript, an Ashoka pillar, a folk-singer
Worksheet — Timeline and Sources of History

activities.description: Hook with a question: 'How do we know that Mohenjo-daro existed 4500 years ago when no one alive saw it?' Take guesses; promise the chapter will answer.
student_actions: Note their guess in the notebook.

activities.description: Roll out a long paper strip on the floor and mark 3000 BCE on the left, 2025 CE on the right. Hand out sticky notes for events: Harappan civilisation, Vedas, Ashoka, Cholas, Mughals, Independence. Students place each note in the right spot.

Cover four blocks: (i) timeline + BCE/CE rules + no year zero; (ii) decade/century/millennium + Ancient/Medieval/Modern; (iii) three families of sources with examples; (iv) stratigraphy + radiocarbon dating.
teacher_actions: Drill the BCE/CE addition rule on the board (100 BCE → 100 CE = 199 yrs).
List Ancient/Medieval/Modern with one example each.
Show pictures of a coin, pot, manuscript, edict, folk-singer and ask which source family.
Sketch layered cake to explain stratigraphy.
student_actions: Sort the picture cards into source families.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions on BCE/CE arithmetic, period-classification of events, source-family sorting, and a short reading on a fictional inscription.
Exit-ticket: 4 quick questions, one from each block.
Homework: ask a grandparent for a family story; classify it as oral source; bring back one detail to share.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (India, that is Bharat).

homework: Compute: how many years between 2500 BCE and 1500 CE?
List THREE objects in your home (or city) that could be a 'source' for a historian 100 years from now. Say which family each belongs to.
Ask a grandparent or older relative for one short family story; write 4–5 lines.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz at the start of next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the layered-excavation problem using the rubric in the answer key.
Peer-grade the family-story homework on whether it has been classified correctly as an oral source.
references: NCERT Class 6 Social Science — Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Chapter 4: Timeline and Sources of History.
